Ayşegül hoca is a nice instructor, they are very knowledgable and easy to communicate. I hope we can see more courses from them about topics like image synthesis. However, although I thought Ercüment hoca was a nice instructor, this semester I completely changed my mind. I hope these things I have listed below were not meant to intentionally suffer the students, but that's what really happened. Here's why I am (and probably many other students are) angry about Ercüment hoca's attitudes:

As a course policy, they do not share the questions solved in the class to encourage people to come to the class. At first, this looks O.K., but when I realized the slides does not cover the material fully enough so that I can grasp what's going on, this policy had no benefit from student's point of view. Since the slides are poorly explaining the concepts, we really require additional readings or materials BEFORE the lectures so that we can follow up. When we cannot follow up the lectures -which indeed many students failed to do so- the ONE simple example solved during the class has no such benefit to us.

They put the homework AND project demo report on the same deadline RIGHT AFTER the midterm week, on monday. First, this is the first time that the report is due before the demo... How meaningless is that... Second, there were a lot of instructors who thoghtfully postponed their deadline (by themselves, without being asked to do so) at least to wednesday so that the students could work on the homework properly. The aim of the homework after all is to teach us those concepts, if I am not going to be able to finish it on time -as many other students also did

I tend to give up some of the questions so that I could compensate the point-loss from the homeword at the midterm.. Also thank you for putting the last homework at the final week again, how thoughtful the course structure is...

That’s because the lecture contents assume as if we are familiar with all those introductory concepts, but we are not… Once I got familiar by reading books and blog posts, then I could understand the lecture slides. But it is too late because instructor will not go over that lecture anymore… As instructors are here to guide us, please consider the class structure once more, moodle slides are not helping us, you may put some helpful links and questions.

In addition, I spent MORE THAN 10 hours just one question of the homework where syllabus says “10 hours per homework”, which is a LIE. If these were group homeworks or every question (one by one, not by overloading) given at every week (not at the half of the semester) then it may be reasonable to say 10 hours per homework. Even though ML is super interesting the course itself is not.

if I spent the same amount of time I wasted on the incredible amount of homework (that the course coordinator has somehow thought was appropriate for a 3 credit course) digging with a shovel, I could dig a hole so deep that I could hand ercüment çiçek over to satan personally. his estimation of how long does it take to finish one homework is nowhere near close to the truth. the syllabus says 10 hours per homework, one QUESTION never takes less than 5. I get that individual study is a big part of this, but I have other classes! I wouldn't even be mad if this course wasn't worth THREE CREDITS, but that's just lying to everyone!! Secondly- the fact that ercüment hoca really moved the progress report and hw1 deadline to ONE DAY AFTER the midterm week just tells you how much he hates his students.
